request: Employees pick a request topic from presets the organization curates (VPN, Claude, Question, Other for staff; Access, Other for clients), and the screens say Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed
note: spec-slice --profile sharded produced 0 shards and left every id S-01..S-58 unassigned, so this pass answered all 58 criteria itself; that is the configured shape and was not chosen here. This branch (build/spec-review) already carries the spec's own implementation — packages/validation/src/request-topics.ts, apps/api/src/requests/request-topics.*, the two migrations, e2e/tests/request-topics.spec.ts — so the currency family was judged two ways: every symbol, message, status, schema fact and cited path the spec names was checked against the tree and holds, and no claim the spec makes about the state before it shipped was treated as stale merely because the spec itself has since been implemented. A frozen spec is never edited to stay current (CLAUDE.md — Writing specs), so nothing was raised on that ground.

findings.claim: the request-detail route that already ships is the one surface the bundle never names, and the detail screen is required to draw a control that only that route can serve

witness.detail: `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}` ships today: apps/api/src/requests/requests.controller.ts:87. The Routes table (contracts:13-22) carries eight rows and none is it, and contracts:24 closes the list explicitly — 'The last three already exist and are amended here' — naming `POST …/requests`, `GET …/requests` and `PATCH …/requests/{requestId}` only. The `topic` member is added in exactly two places and nowhere else: contracts:106-121 ('The `201` body observed today carries … This spec adds one member and removes none', with `topic.name` the snapshot and `topic.status` read from the live row) and contracts:126 ('Each row of `requests[]` gains the same `topic` member'). Against that, the bundle requires the detail screen to render it: contracts:341 makes `request-detail-topic` a required id, 'Request detail | present when the request carries a topic'; contracts:444 requires 'The detail screen renders the snapshot name with a muted "archived" marker beside it', which needs `topic.status`; TC-02-E2E-02 (cases:516,520) asserts 'The list row and the detail header both show `Claude`'; TC-02-E2E-03 (cases:532,534) asserts 'The detail screen shows the snapshot name with the archived marker beside it'. So this is the consequence the register makes blocking rather than a bare missing row — a control the screens draw that no route in this document serves. An implementer who amends exactly the three routes contracts:24 names leaves the detail response without `topic`, and TC-02-E2E-02 and TC-02-E2E-03 both fail. (The two sibling detail ids are not affected: `request-detail-status` and `request-detail-history` are served by the client-side label map of REQ-02-028, which needs no response change.)

findings.suggestedFix: add `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}` to the Routes table as amended, and one line saying its response gains the same `topic` member on the same terms as the `201` body — `topic.name` the snapshot `topicLabel`, the other four read from the row `topicId` names, `topic` null exactly when `topicLabel` is null — so the detail screen's snapshot name and archived marker have a stated source.

findings.claim: two edge cases state a screen behaviour that no case observes

witness.detail: Edge case 2 (contracts:462) has two halves — '`POST …/requests` answers `400` `REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable`' and 'the modal shows the error against the picker'. The first is pinned by TC-02-INT-13 (cases:343-354). The second is not: no case archives a topic while a modal is open and submits from the stale picker; TC-02-E2E-03 (cases:522-534) archives and then re-opens the modal, so it observes the refreshed picker instead. Edge case 10 (contracts:470) likewise says 'The control shows Closed as the nearest selection' for `status=declined` from a saved link; TC-02-INT-17 (cases:404-417) proves the endpoint still accepts `declined`, and no case reads the control's selection. Every other edge case, 1 and 3-9 and 11-15, has a case.

findings.suggestedFix: either fold the stale-picker submission into TC-02-E2E-03 as one extra step and the saved-link selection into TC-02-E2E-04, or add one line to each row saying it has no case and why.

findings.claim: two behaviours requests spec 01 describes are changed here, stated in full and recorded so a person can confirm they were meant

witness.detail: REQ-02-022 (:213) turns `type` and `accessKind` on `POST …/requests` from accepted body fields into a `400` `REQUEST_MESSAGES.classifierNotAccepted`, and contracts:88-92 retires four messages that route emits today — `REQUEST_MESSAGES.typeUnknown`, `accessKindRequired`, `accessKindUnknown`, `accessKindNotAllowed` — all four of which still exist in packages/validation/src/index.ts and are spec 01's. REQ-02-028 (:249) replaces the status words the requests screens show. Both are stated whole in this bundle's own text, spec 01 is neither edited nor marked, and specs/requests/README.md:186,190-193 records the same two changes at area level with their witnesses (TC-02-INT-11, TC-02-UNIT-05). Reported, never blocking: the newest spec governs.

findings.suggestedFix: none. Confirm the retirement of the two body fields was meant to be a hard refusal rather than a deprecation window.

findings.claim: the status-label map is the one shared export the bundle specifies without naming it

witness.detail: REQ-02-028 (:249) requires 'a single exported label map that the list, the detail screen, its history entries and the filter control all read', and contracts:171-187 gives its full contents and says it 'lives beside the messages'. Neither names the export. Every message in the bundle names one — `REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.pickerEmpty`, the twenty rows of the Error Messages table — and TC-02-UNIT-05 (cases:128-137) can only say 'the exported status-label map'. The contents are complete, so this is implementable; it is the one identifier a reader has to invent, and the one an E2E or unit test cannot name.

findings.suggestedFix: name it in the Status Labels heading the way the messages are named, e.g. `REQUEST_STATUS_LABELS` in packages/validation/src/index.ts.

findings.claim: an unknown `audience` on a rename is settled only by reading three places

witness.detail: Rule 2 (contracts:293) is written unscoped — 'topic `audience` | One of `staff`, `client` | `REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.audienceUnknown`' — while rule 3 (contracts:294) is scoped 'on rename'. REQ-02-002 (:100) scopes the unknown-audience refusal to 'a create call or a catalogue read', and the `PATCH …/request-topics/{topicId}` row (contracts:17) lists `audienceImmutable` and not `audienceUnknown`. So `PATCH` with `audience: "partner"` answers `400` `audienceImmutable`, and the answer is determinate — the Routes table settles it. It is filed as a note rather than under S-17 for that reason: the two readings differ only in which `400` message comes back, and the contract closes it. TC-02-INT-06 (cases:232-250) exercises `staff` and `client` on rename and no value outside the set.

findings.suggestedFix: scope rule 2 to the create call and the catalogue read, the way rule 3 is scoped to the rename.

findings.claim: the catalogue read each control makes is named for two of the three controls that make one

witness.detail: REQ-02-031 (:266) names the read behind the requests list's topic filter (`status=all`) and the read behind the new-request picker (`status=active`), and REQ-02-031's Decided says why they must differ. The Settings catalogue screen draws both an active list and an 'Archived' section (contracts:361-375) and no requirement says which read fills it. Unlike R1 the data is reachable — `status=archived` and `status=all` are both declared on the route (contracts:30-34) — so this is a note and not a gap a user meets.

findings.suggestedFix: add the Settings screen to REQ-02-031's sentence: it reads `status=all` and splits the response into the active list and the archived one.

criteriaNotes.S-01: Every symbol named as existing exists under that name: SessionGuard and OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/auth/session.guard.ts, org-scope.guard.ts), apps/api/src/requests/requests.controller.ts and requests.service.ts, normalizeRole in packages/validation/src/roles.ts, the Capability and MemberCapability unions and can() (roles.ts:93,102; index.ts:528,785), @RequireCapability and CapabilityGuard, apps/web/src/ds.ts, the e2e helpers signupOrg/inviteAndAcceptViaApi/setMembershipRole (e2e/tests/helpers.ts:734,921,160), and the suites cited as witnesses — apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts, apps/api/test/org-scope.spec.ts, e2e/tests/holidays.spec.ts (reaches manager), e2e/tests/requests.spec.ts (reaches viewer).
criteriaNotes.S-02: Every quoted message matches its export character for character. All twelve REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES rows and the four new REQUEST_MESSAGES rows match packages/validation/src/index.ts exactly, including pickerEmpty's two sentences; so do the four rows marked 'New: no' — createForbidden, scopeForbidden, fieldImmutable, editForbidden — and the ten field messages listed under POST …/requests, and the four the route is said to stop emitting.
criteriaNotes.S-03: Statuses attributed to shipping routes hold: POST …/requests 201 / 400 / 403 / 404, GET …/requests 200 with the field-keyed `{ "error": "validation_error", "fields": { "status": "unknown_value" } }` body, PATCH …/requests/{requestId} 200 / 400 / 403, and cross-organization 404 rather than 403 (OrgScopeGuard).
criteriaNotes.S-04: Every schema fact holds against apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma: Request keeps `type` and `accessKind` with the five stored statuses; `Client.status` and `Project.status` are documented String columns, which is the precedent the audience column cites; the Client per-organization case-insensitive uniqueness is a hand-written LOWER(name) index (apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260901120000_spec_org_01_clients/migration.sql:26), which is the device the topic's (organizationId, audience, LOWER(name)) index copies.
criteriaNotes.S-05: No 'today the code does X' claim is false. The rehearsal's record that an unknown body member was accepted with 201 is stated in the past tense and is what TC-02-INT-11 turns into a refusal; the claim that '/org/{orgId}/members' is a destination every role can open holds — apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:97-103 adds it unconditionally; the vacation feed's fixed status mapping exists (apps/api/src/requests/vacation-request-feed.service.ts).
criteriaNotes.S-06: Nothing is relied on from @ds that apps/web/src/ds.ts does not export: Button, Modal, Input, Select, Table, Badge and InfoBanner are all there. The two absences are both carried by DS-gaps rows — no sortable/drag primitive and no segmented control — and both claims are true of the barrel; the exported Tabs is bottom-underline navigation (1_DS for dev/components/navigation/Tabs.prompt.md), not a segmented control. The loading skeleton is an app-level pattern already in use (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/members/MembersLoadingSkeleton.tsx), not an @ds export, so it needs no row.
criteriaNotes.S-07: Every premise about the rig is cited rather than restated: the guards, the requests controller and service, the e2e helpers file, the Jest and Playwright suites, and the migration directory the backfill is executed from.
criteriaNotes.S-08: Counts about the document's own contents hold: two decision-table cells and one case exercising both, four write routes, the four null members of `topic`, the five stored statuses, the three refusals TC-02-INT-13 fires, the four rows TC-02-INT-03 creates, the three controls an archived row draws none of.
criteriaNotes.S-09: No pair of requirements resists one implementation. The Actors precondition 'carries at least one active staff topic once seeded' is a starting state, not an invariant, and REQ-02-017 and edge case 13 govern the emptied catalogue; both hold at once.
criteriaNotes.S-10: Requirements, the Routes table, the Error Messages table and every case agree, including the two places it would be easy to drift: the ordering of audienceImmutable before nameDuplicate (contracts:304-307, REQ-02-004, TC-02-INT-06) and the ordering of topicUnavailable before topicAudienceMismatch (REQ-02-019, REQ-02-020's Decided, validation rules 8 and 9, TC-02-INT-12/13).
criteriaNotes.S-11: All sixteen acceptance criteria observe the requirement they name, and each names the case that settles it.
criteriaNotes.S-12: The matrix, the flows and the Routes table agree. `manage-request-topics` is admin and manager, which matches the ManageRequestTopics rows of ROLE_CAPABILITIES (roles.ts:139,174); the catalogue read is granted to all four roles and its route carries no capability; the requester grant is admin/manager/user, matching `user: ['CreateRequest', 'ViewOwnRequests']` and viewer's list without it (roles.ts:180,183). Every grant is used by a flow and every flow's actor is permitted.
criteriaNotes.S-13: Two states, four events, all eight cells present, with the five invariants under them. No edge case names an unreachable state; `active` at creation is invariant 1 rather than a missing row.
criteriaNotes.S-14: No control is drawn for an excluded role — the Settings row and the whole topics page are absent for user and viewer, and the address redirects. The one control drawn without a route to serve it is the detail screen's topic, filed as R1.
criteriaNotes.S-15: Every rule has its data: sortOrder, status, archivedAt, archivedByAccountId, createdByAccountId, the functional unique index and the picker's composite index are all in the Data Model, and every column added is written by a stated rule or the seed.
criteriaNotes.S-16: No rule shadows another. The refusal order is stated where it matters — the topic is found active before its audience is compared, so an archived client topic answers topicUnavailable and not the mismatch; immutability answers before uniqueness; and the create route returns every failing field at once, so no message is unobservable behind another.
criteriaNotes.S-17: No requirement carries two readings that change the implementation. The one that came closest is the unknown `audience` on a rename, which the Routes table settles; it is reported as N4 rather than blocked. Rule 10's 'Absent from the body' likewise settles whether `accessKind: null` is a refusal.
criteriaNotes.S-18: 404 not 403 for a caller outside the organization, stated in the Routes preamble, in Security, and pinned by TC-02-INT-21; the POST …/requests exception answers 400 topicUnavailable and is argued as leaking nothing.
criteriaNotes.S-19: Every user-facing message names a packages/validation export; the only text that is not a validation message, the status labels, is placed in the same package rather than in a screen.
criteriaNotes.S-20: Stated where the rules are stated: the client validates rules 1, 2, 4 and 7, and 'The server re-validates every rule' (contracts:309-313).
criteriaNotes.S-21: 'Submit controls are never disabled for validation — clicking an invalid form shows every error and focuses the first invalid field' (contracts:311-313, UI Description), and TC-02-E2E-02 asserts the control stays enabled on an invalid submit. The in-flight disable while saving is the permitted kind, and REQ-02-017's un-drawn submit is a control that cannot act rather than a disabled one.
criteriaNotes.S-22: Tokens only, named as var(--sp-*) and var(--fs-*), and the two missing primitives go into the DS gaps table rather than being improvised.
criteriaNotes.S-23: No route handler and no server action is asked for; every screen reads /api/....
criteriaNotes.S-24: The Settings row is rendered only for the capability holders and the address is not a destination for anyone else (REQ-02-030, UI Description, TC-02-E2E-05).
criteriaNotes.S-25: Additive: one new table, two nullable columns, no rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL. The backfill is an insert-where-absent and is re-runnable, so the previous code serves through the window.
criteriaNotes.S-26: 'Every check runs against normalizeRole() (packages/validation/src/roles.ts), so legacy `member` maps to `user`', with the matrix given over the target four.
criteriaNotes.S-27: Every route names its guard chain and its capability; the spec revokes no session, so the security stamp is not in play.
criteriaNotes.S-28: Server rules sit at integration — every status, message and authorization decision is an INT case — and the six E2E cases each buy something an API test cannot reach: a modal that keeps its typed value, controls that must not be drawn (up/down on the first and last row, rename on an archived row, the kind controls, the submit on an empty picker), a navigation row that must be absent, focus on an invalid submit, and the same four words across three surfaces. One mechanism, one case.
criteriaNotes.S-29: Selectors are data-testid and all thirty-one ids are named, including the two removed ones.
criteriaNotes.S-30: Covering every mention of another document loses nothing an implementer needs: spec 03 appears only in a Known Gaps 'What closes it' cell, and the references to Client, Project and the clients/holidays surfaces are precedents for a rule this bundle also states in full.
criteriaNotes.S-31: Every route the bundle names states its audience, request, response, statuses and messages. The route it fails to name at all is R1, filed under S-58 rather than counted twice here.
criteriaNotes.S-32: The two behaviours changed from requests spec 01 are stated whole here — the retired classifier with its four no-longer-emitted messages, and the status vocabulary — and spec 01 is neither edited nor marked. Recorded as N2 under S-57.
criteriaNotes.S-33: The vocabularies are enumerated exhaustively: audience staff|client, kind access|question, status active|archived, the catalogue read's active|archived|all, and the stored-status-to-label map with its closure sub-labels.
criteriaNotes.S-34: No TBD, no 'decide later'; every requirement states behaviour, and each Decided names the alternative it rejected.
criteriaNotes.S-35: No external system. The Access table says so in one row — no third-party system, no API key, no MCP server, no mail — and no row is marked Assumed.
criteriaNotes.S-58: Blocked by R1: GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId} ships today and can serve a request carrying this spec's new topic member, and the bundle neither amends it nor places it out of scope, while requiring the detail screen to draw request-detail-topic and the archived marker. The other shipping surfaces are answered: PATCH …/requests/{requestId} by REQ-02-024, GET …/requests and POST …/requests by the amended contracts, the requests-type-filter by contracts:428-430, and the vacation section by contracts:189-196.
criteriaNotes.S-36: Every case's steps reach the state it asserts under the spec's own rules, including the two that looked doubtful: TC-02-INT-02 deletes the topic rows, which SetNull leaves as a topicLabel with no topicId — exactly the state contracts:118-121 describes — and TC-02-INT-03's clamping produces the order its expected result claims against the seeded values 10..90.
criteriaNotes.S-37: Every expected result follows from its steps; TC-02-INT-16's two halves each name the mechanism that produces the answer, the row lock and the functional unique index.
criteriaNotes.S-38: Each acceptance criterion is settled by a stated observation and none restates its requirement; the three that name two observers name one per level, which the Verification Plan's table repeats.
criteriaNotes.S-39: The case amended for the new contract, TC-02-INT-11, is amended on both halves: the steps send the retired classifier and the expected result is the refusal plus an unchanged count.
criteriaNotes.S-40: The Verification Plan records routes, states and observers only — a container name and 'the E2E database', never a port, a database name or a connection string; the suite is recorded as claiming its own port pair.
criteriaNotes.S-41: Everything the request asked for is covered: the curated presets including VPN, Claude, Question and Other for staff and Access and Other for clients, the employee's pick, and Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed on the list, the detail header, its history and the filter.
criteriaNotes.S-42: The additions beyond the request that need naming are named in the Summary: the topic becoming the only classifier a caller supplies, `accessKind` no longer accepted, and the list's topic filter. The wider seed is argued in its own Decided.
criteriaNotes.S-43: The unconditional invariants were checked against the call sites they govern: apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:601 is the only creator of a Request row, so REQ-02-018, REQ-02-021 and REQ-02-023 have one call site and no violator; there is no second writer of topicLabel.
criteriaNotes.S-44: Every requirement has a case that fails if it is implemented backwards, and the ones about drawn controls have both directions — REQ-02-030 present in TC-02-E2E-01 and absent in TC-02-E2E-05, REQ-02-017 empty in TC-02-E2E-06 and populated in TC-02-E2E-02, REQ-02-007 refused for user and granted for manager in one case.
criteriaNotes.S-45: Every message and refusal has an Error Messages row naming its export and its route, and the one row with no route, pickerEmpty, says in the line under the table why it has none.
criteriaNotes.S-46: Every ## section has a case; two edge cases have only half of theirs — N1.
criteriaNotes.S-47: Fifteen numbered edge cases, each with exact behaviour.
criteriaNotes.S-48: The Summary points at specs/requests/README.md for blast radius and backward compatibility, and that file carries both for spec 02 rather than repeating them here.
criteriaNotes.S-49: Known Gaps is five rows over why-acceptable and what-closes-it; Out of Scope is five entries each saying what happens instead.
criteriaNotes.S-50: Every asserted-absent has a presence twin in another case — the settings tab, the topics page, the add control, the submit and the picker — and the two removed ids are declared removed rather than asserted absent against a twin that cannot exist.
